# Hydra Sync 1.10.0

Five known limitations removed: achievements show up without a restart, undo only takes back what
Hydra Sync added, an additive playtime mode, achievement metadata for games with no AppID, and
merging with data Playnite Achievements already has.

## What's new

### New achievements appear without restarting Playnite

Previously a sync wrote the unlocks and waited for Playnite Achievements to pick them up at its next
start, which meant restarting Playnite to see anything new. Hydra Sync now asks Playnite
Achievements to apply them straight away, and its views refresh without a restart. When Playnite
Achievements can't be reached — not installed, or not loaded yet — nothing changes for the worse:
the file is written and applied at its next start as before, and you get one notification saying so.

Toggle: **Show new achievements without restarting Playnite** (on by default).

### Undo only removes Hydra Sync's contribution

**Undo playtime changes…** used to put a game's playtime back to the value captured before the
extension first touched it, which also discarded anything Playnite recorded in the meantime. It now
subtracts exactly what Hydra Sync added and keeps the rest, so sessions you played after a sync
survive, undoing twice is harmless, and a later sync is just as undoable as the first. The
confirmation dialog says so.

### Additive playtime mode

A new **Playtime** setting picks the rule:

| Mode | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Hydra wins (replace when larger)** *(default, unchanged)* | A game is only ever raised to Hydra's cumulative total, and only when Hydra's is higher |
| **Add Hydra's new playtime since the previous sync** | Keeps your Playnite total and adds whatever Hydra gained |

The additive mode records where Hydra's playtime stood on the first pass and changes nothing on that
pass, so it can never double-count. Switching between the modes is safe for the same reason: the
previous Hydra figure is always recorded.

### Achievement metadata for games with no AppID

Games whose AppID can't be discovered (typically non-Steam Hydra entries) had no way to get real
achievement names, descriptions and icons. They're now looked up by title on the store, and the
matching is strict enough that sequels and similarly-named games won't be confused. Lookups are
cached for 30 days, and the definition file in the game folder still wins when there is one.

### Merging with Playnite Achievements instead of replacing it

Hydra Sync used to overwrite whatever Playnite Achievements had stored for a game. It now merges:
achievements from other sources are kept, an unlocked achievement never goes back to locked, and
metadata is refreshed only for entries that came from the same source. Unlocks with no metadata
behind them are kept rather than dropped. Toggle: **Merge with existing Playnite Achievements
data** (on by default; turn it off for the previous behaviour).

## Upgrade notes

- Nothing is re-synced and no state is lost — upgrading is safe at any time. The first sync after
  updating behaves like any other.
- If you use the default *Hydra wins* mode, playtime behaviour is unchanged.
- Undo now keeps post-sync playtime. If you were relying on undo to also discard sessions played
  after a sync, set **Playtime** to *Add Hydra's new playtime* and use undo right after a sync
  instead.
- Both new achievement settings are on by default, so no action is needed to get the restart-free
  behaviour and merging.
- In *Add Hydra's new playtime* mode the first sync for each game records a starting point and adds
  nothing; the sync notification says how many games that applied to.

## Install

1. Download `HydraSync-1.10.0.pext` from the [Releases page](https://github.com/cometmcisaac/hydra-playnite-sync/releases).
2. Double-click it and confirm the update in Playnite, or extract the contents into
   `%APPDATA%\Playnite\Extensions\A76358E9-BFA2-4189-B6F3-2307EA4E217B\`.
3. Restart Playnite.

Settings live under **Add-ons → Extensions settings → Generic → Hydra Sync**. Two in-app reports
(`Diagnose achievement sync…` and `Diagnose HowLongToBeat playtime sync…` on a game's context menu)
now also report whether achievements were applied immediately, whether they were merged, and which
playtime mode is active.
